pointers.sentence: It raises `ValueError` where `FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN` finds a quotation mark (single, double, a backtick or a square bracket), whitespace, a control character, a semicolon, a hash, or a comment marker, `"--"`, `"/*"` or `"*/"` (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.check_alias`).

The compiler writes the alias in quotation marks with the backend's `quote_name`, which on PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL wraps a name not already wrapped and escapes nothing inside it (`django/db/backends/postgresql/operations.py:DatabaseOperations.quote_name`).

The name of a `FilteredRelation` becomes the alias of the table its join brings in, where that table is not yet in the query (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.table_alias`); `Join.as_sql` writes the alias after the table (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`).

The name of a `FilteredRelation` becomes the alias of the table its join brings in, where that table is not yet in the query (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.table_alias`); `Join.as_sql` writes the alias after the table (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`).

At this commit `add_filtered_relation` refuses a name with a period, and the compiler writes a dotted name that way only when it was given to `extra` as its order_by (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler._order_by_pairs`).

`Q.__init__` takes two keyword arguments of its own beside the conditions, `"_connector"` and `"_negated"`, and the connector is the word that `WhereNode.as_sql` writes between the conditions it joins (`django/db/models/sql/where.py:WhereNode.as_sql`).

`Q._check_connector` refuses with `ValueError` any connector but `Q.AND`, `Q.OR`, `Q.XOR` and `None`, in the constructor and, at this commit, in `Q.create` (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q._check_connector`).

`QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace` refuses both with `TypeError`, by the set `PROHIBITED_FILTER_KWARGS`, and at this commit `When.__init__` does the same (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace`; [`filter`, `exclude` and `Q` objects](../querysets/filters.md)).
On Oracle a JSON path cannot be a bind variable, the comments in the JSON lookups say, so the lookups write it into the statement (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:HasKeyLookup`).
At this commit `HasKeyLookup.as_oracle` writes only the path and passes the left-hand side's parameters as bind variables (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:HasKeyLookup.as_oracle`).

A comment says that each key of the path passes through `json.dumps`, which writes U+FFFF as an escape, and the path stands in an Oracle literal delimited by U+FFFF, so that the delimiter is never in it (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:ProcessJSONLHSMixin._process_as_oracle`; [The SQL a backend writes: `BaseDatabaseOperations`](../backends/operations.md)).

A raster lookup on PostGIS may carry a band index in its value (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/lookups.py:GISLookup.process_band_indices`), and `PostGISOperator.check_raster` writes the index into the SQL beside its operand.

Since 5.2.11 and 6.0.2 (CVE-2026-1207) it raises `TypeError` for an index that is not an integer (`django/contrib/gis/db/backends/postgis/operations.py:PostGISOperator.check_raster`; [Spatial lookups, functions and distances](../contrib/spatial-queries.md)).
